title: Rescheduling an Overridden Instance Across Another Occurrence or Split Boundary (RECURRENCE-ID vs DTSTART Ordering)

citations.verbatim_quote:
The DATE-TIME value is set to the time when the original recurrence instance would occur; meaning that if the intent is to change a Friday meeting to Thursday, the DATE-TIME is still set to the original Friday meeting.

      The "RECURRENCE-ID" property is used in conjunction with the "UID" and "SEQUENCE" properties to identify a particular instance of a recurring event, to-do, or journal.  For a given pair of "UID" and "SEQUENCE" property values, the "RECURRENCE-ID" value for a recurrence instance is fixed.
Subsequent instances are determined by their "RECURRENCE-ID" value and not their current scheduled start time.

The "Organizer" can identify a specific recurrence instance using the "RECURRENCE-ID" property.  The property value is equal to the date/time of the instance.  If the "Organizer" wishes to change the "DTSTART", the original, unmodified "DTSTART" value of the instance is used as the value "RECURRENCE-ID" property, and the new "DTSTART" and "DTEND" values reflect the change.

rationale: RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.4 and RFC 5546 Section 3.7.1 decouple an overridden occurrence's logical identity in the recurrence set (`RECURRENCE-ID`, which is fixed to the original unmodified occurrence start time) from its actual scheduled start time (`DTSTART`). As RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.4 explicitly illustrates, when a Friday instance is rescheduled to Thursday—potentially before an earlier occurrence in the same series—its `RECURRENCE-ID` remains the original Friday timestamp while its `DTSTART` becomes Thursday. Furthermore, RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.4 mandates that for `RANGE=THISANDFUTURE` operations, 'Subsequent instances are determined by their RECURRENCE-ID value and not their current scheduled start time.' This creates a dual-ordering invariant: (1) chronological timeline queries order the overridden occurrence by its new `DTSTART` (even when moved earlier than `T1` or later than `T3`), whereas (2) recurrence-set identity operations (re-editing/deleting by `recurrence_id`, suppressing the original slot `T2` during master expansion, and determining whether `T2 >= split_rid` in a `THIS_AND_FUTURE` operation) are governed strictly by `RECURRENCE-ID = T2`.
store_implication:
1. When occurrence `T2` of a recurring series is edited with `Range=NONE` to a new `DTSTART = T_new` that precedes an earlier occurrence `T1` (`T_new < T1 < T2`) or follows a later occurrence `T3` (`T2 < T3 < T_new`), the override component MUST keep `RECURRENCE-ID = T2` and `DTSTART = T_new`.
2. During timeline expansion, the override component replaces the master occurrence at `T2` (not `T1` or `T3`), and the emitted occurrences on the timeline MUST be ordered chronologically by their effective `DTSTART` (so `T_new` appears before `T1` if `T_new < T1`, with `recurrence_id = T2`).
3. During a subsequent `THIS_AND_FUTURE` edit or delete at `split_rid`, whether the rescheduled override is included in the future range `[split_rid, ...)` MUST be determined by comparing its `RECURRENCE-ID` (`T2 >= split_rid`), NOT its rescheduled `DTSTART` (`T_new >= split_rid`).
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Rescheduling the 2nd occurrence (`T2 = May 2 09:00`) to `T0 = April 30 09:00` (before the master's initial `DTSTART = May 1 09:00`): timeline expansion MUST emit `[April 30 (recurrence_id=May 2), May 1 (recurrence_id=May 1), May 3 (recurrence_id=May 3)]`. A query window covering April 30 MUST include the rescheduled override even though the master's `DTSTART` is May 1.

Subsequent THIS_AND_FUTURE delete at `split_rid = May 2 09:00` when the May 2 override was moved earlier to `April 30 09:00`: because its `RECURRENCE-ID` (`May 2 09:00`) is `>= split_rid`, the May 2 override MUST be removed by the `THIS_AND_FUTURE` deletion even though its rescheduled `DTSTART` (`April 30`) is earlier than May 2.

Subsequent THIS_AND_FUTURE delete at `split_rid = May 3 09:00` when the May 2 override (`RECURRENCE-ID = May 2 09:00`) was moved later to `May 4 09:00`: because its `RECURRENCE-ID` (`May 2 09:00`) is `< split_rid`, the May 2 override is a prior instance (not a subsequent instance per RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.4) and MUST be preserved.

Rescheduling an occurrence `T2` to the exact same `DTSTART` wall-clock time as another occurrence `T1` (`T_new == T1`): both occurrences remain distinct in the recurrence set because their `(UID, RECURRENCE-ID)` keys are `(UID, T1)` and `(UID, T2)`, and both are emitted on the timeline at `T1`.
